To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the growth rate of an aggregate series is not equal to the growth rate of the sum of its components; (ii) indirect seasonal adjustment is preferable to direct seasonal adjustment of an aggregated series, and (iii) growth rates of seasonally adjusted series are not additive.
indirect seasonal adjustment should be preferred over direct seasonal adjustment in the case of aggregation of seasonally-adjusted series.

the indirect approach is preferable to direct seasonal adjustment; the differences between direct and indirect adjusted growth rates are significant and can be large; the differences between the direct and indirect growth rates can be reduced by applying a different method of seasonal adjustment to the components; the differences between growth rates of direct and indirect seasonally adjusted series are larger in the first years after the break in the seasonal pattern than in the later years.
